tracks.title: Hold The Line Open
tracks.subject: a long-distance call
tracks.caption: An indie rock band recorded live in one room — drums, bass and two electric guitars, one clean and arpeggiated, one with light overdrive. A raspy male voice sings close-miked and conversational in the verses and pushes into a shout on the chorus. Bone-dry drums with audible room bleed, no reverb on the vocal, tape saturation on the bus. Driving, 132 BPM, E minor. Urgent, unresolved.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - Guitars]

[Verse 1]
Eight hours and a bad connection
You say my name and then it cuts
I hold the phone against the window
Like the glass could help somehow

[Pre-Chorus]
Don't hang up yet
Don't hang up yet

[Chorus]
Hold the line open
Even if there's nothing on it
I'd rather hear you breathing wrong
Than hear the room without you in it

[Verse 2]
You're asleep before my morning
I'm asleep before your night
We trade the same four hours over
Like they're all we're allowed

[Guitar Solo]

[Bridge]
I counted every time it dropped
I stopped at forty-one
I kept redialing anyway

[Chorus]
Hold the line open
Even if there's nothing on it
I'd rather hear you breathing wrong
Than hear the room without you in it

[Outro]
Still here
Still here

tracks.title: Somebody Left The Porch Light
tracks.subject: coming home after a long absence
tracks.caption: Gospel soul. Hammond organ through a rotating speaker, upright piano, bass, live kit, tambourine on two and four, hand claps. A powerful female lead sings with heavy melisma and full-chest belting; a choir answers every line in call and response and stacks harmonies under the final chorus, which modulates up a semitone. Recorded live in a room with natural bleed and long gospel-room reverb. 92 BPM, E-flat major. Rising, communal, grateful.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - Organ]

[Verse 1]
Seven years is a long walk back
I counted every mile in my chest
The mailbox leans the way it always leaned
And somebody left the porch light on

[Pre-Chorus]
(Still burning) still burning
(Still waiting) still waiting

[Chorus]
Somebody left the porch light on
After everything I said
I don't deserve that yellow square of glass
But Lord, I'm walking to it anyway

[Verse 2]
My mother's hands are smaller now
She don't ask me where I've been
She just puts another plate down
Like I never left the room

[Bridge - Choir]
(Come on home) come on home
(Come on home) I'm coming

[Chorus - key change]
Somebody left the porch light on
After everything I said
I don't deserve that yellow square of glass
But Lord, I'm walking to it anyway

[Outro]
Still burning
Still burning

tracks.title: Two Lanes Out Of Tulsa
tracks.subject: a two-lane road out of town
tracks.caption: Country rock in the Nashville tradition. Acoustic guitar and a Telecaster trading fills, pedal steel sustaining under every vocal line, fiddle taking the solo, Hammond organ pad, bass and a relaxed shuffle on the kit. A male baritone sings with a pronounced twang and southern drawl, conversational and unhurried, with a low harmony on the choruses. Warm analog saturation, plate reverb, slapback on the vocal. 98 BPM, G major. Nostalgic, dusty, unhurried.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - Pedal Steel]

[Verse 1]
Two lanes out of Tulsa and a radio
Playing something my father would've known
The girl at the Conoco called me honey
And I about came apart

[Pre-Chorus]
It don't take much these days

[Chorus]
I ain't running, I'm just driving
There's a difference if you've done both
One of them's got somewhere to be
And one of them just needs the road

[Verse 2]
There's a church sign outside Sapulpa
Says the Lord ain't finished with you yet
Well I hope He's got some patience left
Because I'm slower than most

[Fiddle Solo]

[Chorus]
I ain't running, I'm just driving
There's a difference if you've done both
One of them's got somewhere to be
And one of them just needs the road

[Outro]
Just needs the road
Just needs the road

tracks.title: Rearview Saint
tracks.subject: driving too fast at night
tracks.caption: Phonk with darker cinematic textures. A distorted 808 sub bass sliding between notes, the signature cowbell melody, chopped and pitched vocal samples, a filtered string swell under the second half, no live drums. A low male voice half-speaks the lines, heavily doubled and slightly distorted, with reversed ad-libs in the gaps. Dusty vinyl texture over a punchy modern low end. 150 BPM, G minor. Fast, dark, propulsive.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - Cowbell]

[Verse 1]
Ninety on a road built for fifty
Saint on the dash that I don't believe in
He's been facing backwards seven years
Watching where I've already been

[Hook]
Rearview saint, rearview saint
Won't you look the other way
Everything ahead of me
Is nothing I can pray about

[Verse 2]
City's just a smear of orange
Radio's a language I don't speak
Every exit's got my name on it
I take none of them

[Hook]
Rearview saint, rearview saint
Won't you look the other way
Everything ahead of me
Is nothing I can pray about

[Outro - reversed]
Look the other way

tracks.title: Smoke Without A Room
tracks.subject: an apartment emptied of furniture
tracks.caption: Trip hop in the Bristol tradition, with a modern revival edge. A dusty swung breakbeat sampled from vinyl, upright bass, a muted trumpet answering the vocal, a Rhodes playing two chords, continuous crackle. A smoky female alto sings very close to the mic, breathy and understated, never raising her voice, with a whispered double an octave down. Lo-fi intimacy, no bright highs, tape hiss throughout. 86 BPM, A minor. Late, hollow, beautiful.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - Breakbeat]

[Verse 1]
The sofa left a rectangle
Cleaner than the rest of the floor
Eight years of not moving anything
Printed on the carpet

[Pre-Chorus]
I keep walking into rooms
To look at nothing

[Chorus]
It's smoke without a room now
It's a shape where a thing used to be
I could paint over all of it
But then I'd have to pick a colour

[Verse 2]
Your key still opens the door
I checked, I don't know why
The lock doesn't know anything's changed
Lucky lock

[Trumpet Solo]

[Chorus]
It's smoke without a room now
It's a shape where a thing used to be
I could paint over all of it
But then I'd have to pick a colour

[Outro]
Lucky lock
Lucky lock

tracks.title: The Weight Of Small Hours
tracks.subject: sitting up with someone who is ill
tracks.caption: Contemporary folk, almost entirely acoustic. Fingerpicked steel-string guitar in an open tuning, upright bass entering in the second verse, brushed percussion, a single cello line under the bridge. A soft male tenor sings barely above a whisper, extremely close-miked so the breath is audible, with a wordless female harmony joining the last chorus. Tape saturation, no reverb on the lead vocal, room tone left in. 74 BPM, C major. Tender, still, unsentimental.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - Fingerpicked Guitar]

[Verse 1]
The machine counts something out loud
Every four seconds, all night
I've started breathing along with it
Which I know is not useful

[Pre-Chorus]
You asked me once to stop fussing
So I'll just sit

[Chorus]
This is the weight of small hours
It isn't heavy, it's just long
I'd carry something heavier gladly
If anybody offered me the choice

[Verse 2]
The nurse has a good laugh
She uses it on purpose
She knows exactly what it's for
And it works, it works on me

[Cello - Bridge]

[Chorus - with harmony]
This is the weight of small hours
It isn't heavy, it's just long
I'd carry something heavier gladly
If anybody offered me the choice

[Outro]
Just long
Just long
